what: Replace better-sqlite3 with sql.js for telemetry
why: Native C++ addon cannot be bundled by esbuild; marketplace installs lack node_modules. sql.js is pure WASM and bundles cleanly.

what: Use nullish coalescing for env passthrough in spawn
why: Spread merge ({ ...process.env, ...options.env }) restores deleted keys. Use options.env ?? process.env to trust caller's env as-is.

what: Replace 173 unused tech-specific skills with 25 outcome-oriented skills in 4-tier architecture
why: Zero usage across 4186 sessions. Skills should teach agent behavior patterns, not describe technologies.

what: All skills must have scripts/ and references/ folders with content per Anthropic spec
why: Progressive disclosure: frontmatter (description) -> SKILL.md body (instructions) -> references/ (detailed material). Scripts provide deterministic validation.

what: Validation scripts must be POSIX-portable: set -euo pipefail, printf not echo -e, no GNU extensions, -- before filename args
why: Scripts must work on macOS (BSD) and Linux. GNU-only sed/grep extensions cause silent failures on BSD.

what: Config restructured from flat dot-notation keys to nested object format for service registry
why: Service registry reads config.fetch.services (nested), but precision_config set with dot-notation keys creates flat keys. Using addService() or full nested object prevents the bug.

what: OpenAI service uses ChatGPT Product API (chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/) not Developer API (api.openai.com/v1/)
why: OAuth tokens from Codex CLI Auth0 PKCE flow have OIDC scopes only, not API scopes. Developer API requires sk-... keys. Product API accepts ChatGPT OAuth tokens.

what: Added format/mode alias resolution to precision_glob and precision_symbols handlers
why: MCP schema defines output.format but handlers read output.mode. Nullish coalescing chain checks both.

what: Use regex /^[^*?{}[]]+\\/.test(p) for subdirectory pattern detection instead of p.includes('/')
why: p.includes('/') catches **/*.ts patterns which work fine in ripgrep, causing unnecessary performance regression

what: Added tree-sitter to TS compiler fallback chain in precision_symbols processFile()
why: tree-sitter can fail for various reasons but dead extractSymbols() function using TS compiler API works reliably for TS/JS files

what: Duplicate shellEscape() in process-manager.ts matching precision-exec.ts for consistent background spawn escaping
why: Harmonizes foreground and background argument escaping. Small function (8 lines) makes duplication acceptable over adding a shared utility.

what: Added cell_id targeting to precision_notebook as optional alternative to index-based targeting
why: Index-based targeting is fragile in batch operations (insert shifts subsequent indices). cell_id provides stable targeting using nbformat 4.5+ cell IDs with metadata.id fallback.

what: cell_id takes precedence over index when both are provided, with warning logged
why: Predictable precedence avoids ambiguity. cell_id is more stable than index, so it should win. Backward compatible since cell_id is purely additive.

what: Skill instructions must match actual code interfaces - secrets file uses services.<name> (no fetch prefix) with ServiceAuth objects
why: Skill had fetch.services.<name> with api_key field, but code expects services.<name> with type/token/key fields. Mismatch caused 401 auth failures.

what: precision_config only supports get/set/reload - use read-modify-write pattern for deletions
why: No delete action exists. To remove a config key: read parent object, delete key, write back via set.

what: Absorb batch engine concepts into precision engine v2 instead of fixing batch delegation
why: Batch engine reimplements everything (raw fs.readFile, child_process.exec) instead of delegating. Zero usage in production (batches_completed: 0). The concepts are sound but architecture is wrong.

what: Reject checkpoint system in favor of git + precision_edit atomic rollback
why: precision_edit already covers ~80-90% of rollback cases with atomic transactions. Git handles cross-call persistence. No value in custom snapshot infrastructure.

what: SQLite telemetry (better-sqlite3) with zero LLM token cost — only precision_id returned to model
why: Server-side recording avoids bloating LLM context with telemetry data. precision_id is ~1 token for correlation. Token estimates (payload/4) retained for future budget engine.

what: Session state in separate files (.goodvibes/state/session_{id}.json), NOT in goodvibes.json
why: goodvibes.json is config-only. Ephemeral session data would bloat it massively. Separate files enable per-session isolation and easy cleanup.

what: 4 unified hook events (PrePrecisionTool, PostPrecisionTool, OnPrecisionError, OnPrecisionMutation) with filter-based scoping
why: CamelCase matches Claude Code convention. Filter by tool_name instead of per-tool events. Adding new tools never requires new hook events.

what: Delete restricted to project root (git root with cwd fallback) in precision_exec file_ops
why: Copy and move may legitimately work with external paths. Delete is destructive — restrict to project boundary for safety. Use Bash rm for paths outside project.

what: Agent dossier is structured JSON supplement to orchestrator instructions, NOT a replacement
why: Orchestrator writes WHAT to do in natural language. Dossier provides HOW, context, and constraints. output_format is optional — only for when exact response structure is needed.

what: Mode system moved to precision_config, not removed — modes live in config enforcement, not prompts
why: Modes currently work via prompt but config enforcement adds guarantees. Lower priority but kept in design.

what: Telemetry uses SQLite via better-sqlite3, not JSON files
why: Append-only structured data with query capabilities, zero overhead for synchronous writes, WAL mode for concurrent reads

what: Session state stored in separate files (.goodvibes/state/), not in goodvibes.json
why: Keeps goodvibes.json for configuration only. Ephemeral session data in isolated files prevents config bloat and cross-session interference.

what: precision_id format: {tool}_{session_short}_{unique_id} with 8-char hex components
why: Human-readable correlation IDs. Tool prefix for quick filtering, session for grouping, unique for dedup. Zero LLM token cost — server-side only.

what: PrecisionRuntime singleton coordinates all subsystems: config, state, telemetry, index, session
why: Scattered singletons needed unified lifecycle management. Handler dispatch wrapper generates precision_id, records telemetry, and prepends ID to responses. Graceful degradation ensures tools work without runtime.

what: 4 unified hook events (PrePrecisionTool, PostPrecisionTool, OnPrecisionError, OnPrecisionMutation) with filter-based tool scoping
why: CamelCase matches Claude Code convention. Filter by tool_name instead of per-tool events. Adding new tools never requires new hook events. Built-in hooks active by default even without config.

what: precision_agent uses stdin (temp file + shell redirect) for prompt delivery, not CLI positional args
why: CLI positional args have OS ARG_MAX limits (~128KB-2MB). Prompts with dossier + context files can easily exceed this. Shell redirect `< file` avoids the limit entirely.

what: FORBIDDEN_CLI_FLAGS blocklist prevents user override of security-critical flags in precision_agent
why: cli_flags is a pass-through escape hatch. Without blocklist, users could override --model, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --print, --stdin. Blocklist includes short aliases (m, p).

what: DPB naming retained, not renamed to GPA — precision_apply was not built
why: GPA (Gather-Plan-Apply) required precision_apply tool. precision_apply deferred to future work. DPB naming is established across all docs and agent files.
